text: In diabetes, Farxiga/Forxiga is a global leader in the SGLT2 class of diabetes treatments with a 35% volume share. Product Sales of Brilinta/Brilique reached $839 million and in many countries it is the leading medicine for patients discharged with acute coronary syndrome.
justification: This argument focuses on the company's current product sales performance and market leadership in specific therapeutic areas.

text: Since its launch at the end of 2014, we have treated nearly 5,000 cancer patients with Lynparza and launched it in 31 countries with seven ongoing reviews.
justification: This argument highlights the product launch and clinical reach of Lynparza, emphasizing its adoption and regulatory progress.

text: As we look ahead to 2017 and beyond, continued investment in our pipeline keeps us on track to return to sustainable growth in line with our targets. Cambridge, along with Gaithersburg, MD, US and Gothenburg in Sweden, is one of our three strategic R&D centres and it also became our global corporate headquarters in May 2016. Our activities there demonstrate our focus on science, collaborative way of working and commitment to sustainability.
justification: This argument outlines the company's forward-looking investment strategy in R&D infrastructure and its alignment with long-term growth and sustainability goals.

text: 2016 was a crucial year in the second stage of our journey, as we manage a transitional period of patent expiries, drive our Growth Platforms and roll out our new medicines. Between 2011 and 2016, Product Sales in Established Markets of brands that have lost exclusivity, including Crestor, Nexium and Seroquel, have reduced from $20 billion to $6 billion. Unfavourable currency movements account for $2 billion of this $14 billion reduction. This decline represents a significant ‘headwind’, but we have made significant progress rebuilding our Company for the future and preparing for a new period of growth driven by our pipeline delivery.
justification: This argument discusses the strategic challenge of patent expiries and the company's response to rebuild and prepare for future growth.

text: In parallel to managing our legacy brands decline, we have launched a significant number of new medicines and increased revenues from our recently launched medicines. For example, Tagrisso was only launched in November 2015 and became our biggest lung cancer medicine during the year.
justification: This argument presents operational performance data showing revenue growth from new product launches offsetting legacy declines.

text: In 2016, we had four regional approvals, seven expedited reviews and seven regulatory submissions for our Oncology medicines. Looking ahead, we have the potential to deliver our third Oncology medicine in 2017 – halfway to our 2020 target in just four years.
justification: This argument focuses on product development progress and regulatory milestones in the Oncology pipeline.

text: In 2016, we voluntarily withdrew the marketing authorisation application submitted to the EMA for cediranib in advanced ovarian cancer. However, there remain ongoing studies to investigate cediranib as a combination partner with Lynparza and other compounds. In addition, three of our Oncology trials failed to meet their primary endpoints. Another development showed our Values in action. In clinical trials of durvalumab for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, we observed bleeding events. Following the precautionary principle, we placed a voluntary hold on enrolment of new patients, followed by a partial clinical hold from the FDA. After providing a comprehensive analysis, the FDA’s hold was subsequently lifted.
justification: This argument addresses setbacks and regulatory challenges in clinical trials, highlighting risk management and patient safety considerations.

text: In 2016, our Cardiovascular & Metabolic Disease team saw three approvals, four regulatory submissions and two Brilinta trials which failed to meet their primary endpoints. We received a complete response letter from the FDA for ZS-9 for the treatment of hyperkalaemia and subsequently made a resubmission. Positive results from our DURATION-8 trials demonstrated the efficacy of Farxiga and Bydureon in combination for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes and should help us maximise the value of our Diabetes portfolio.
justification: This argument details product development outcomes, regulatory interactions, and clinical trial results in Cardiovascular & Metabolic Disease and Diabetes.

text: During the year, Bevespi Aerosphere was approved in the US and launched in early 2017. Our Respiratory team also made three regulatory submissions, including two for benralizumab for treating severe, uncontrolled asthma. We believe benralizumab, which would be our first Respiratory biologic, will become an important medicine for patients with severe asthma and potentially COPD, as well as an important growth driver for our Company, broadening and deepening our offering in the Respiratory market.
justification: This argument focuses on new product approvals, launches, and pipeline potential in the Respiratory therapy area.

text: Business development and collaboration are at the heart of the way AstraZeneca operates. In 2016, we entered into collaborations to maximise the potential of key products outside our main therapy areas and bring them to patients quicker. Examples include agreements with LEO Pharma for brodalumab and tralokinumab, and with Allergan for MEDI2070. In Alzheimer’s disease, together with Lilly, we obtained a Fast Track Designation for the BACE inhibitor and entered a second collaboration to co-develop MEDI1814. We are also partnering some in-line products with growth potential but without promotional support, such as the agreement with China Medical System Holdings for Plendil in China. We have been divesting smaller non-core products to reinvest value in our pipeline, creating more long-term value through our main therapy areas.
justification: This argument describes strategic partnerships, collaborations, and portfolio management to enhance pipeline and long-term value.

text: Since announcing our science-led strategy in 2013, we set ambitious pipeline targets for the end of 2016. We aimed for nine to 10 new molecular entities (NMEs) in Phase III or registration and achieved 12. We targeted eight to 10 new medicines and major line extension regulatory approvals in 2015 to 2016 and achieved eight, a significant improvement compared to historical performance. We also reshaped our research and early development efforts to produce a steady stream of new products to support long-term growth, achieving 25 Phase II starts in 2015 to 2016, exceeding our target of 12 to 16. Looking ahead, we expect an unprecedented number of submissions in the next 24 months, with around half in Oncology. In April, we announced plans to sharpen prioritisation of investments in our main therapy areas, particularly Oncology, and increase partnering in inflammation, infection and neuroscience. We also aligned costs and streamlined operations.
justification: This argument outlines the company’s strategic pipeline targets, achievements, and future investment prioritisation to drive growth.

text: Our Return to growth is underpinned by our Growth Platforms. As our strategy has progressed, our Growth Platforms have evolved – New Oncology was added and from January 2017, New CVMD combined our Diabetes and Brilinta/Brilique Platforms. As diabetes treatment focuses more on cardiovascular risk reduction, we see clear synergies managing diabetes and Brilinta/Brilique together. Despite increasing competition, pricing pressures and geopolitical instability, Growth Platforms grew by 4% at actual exchange rates (5% at CER) and now represent 63% of all revenues. Emerging Markets are particularly important, supported by China’s growth of 4% (10% at CER) to $2,636 million. Brilinta/Brilique sales grew by 36% (39% at CER) to $839 million. Respiratory sales declined by 8% (6% at CER) reflecting US pricing pressure for Symbicort. New Oncology had strong sales of $664 million, with Tagrisso delivering sales of $175 million in its first full year. US revenue was down 22% to $7,365 million; Europe down 5% to $5,064 million; and Established ROW rose by 2% to $3,096 million.
justification: This argument provides detailed financial and operational performance metrics for the company’s Growth Platforms and regional revenues.

text: Employee opinion surveys help us measure satisfaction and engagement and how we are doing in our aim to be a great place to work. Our most recent survey in December 2016 showed a decline compared to our very high 2015 score, although results are in line with the ‘global pharma norm’. This decline might not be unexpected given the challenges of the strategic journey and restructuring in 2016 as we continued losing sales to patent expiries. Nevertheless, we are focused on improving performance in areas employees tell us are important drivers of engagement, including people development and line manager communication.
justification: This argument addresses employee engagement and internal culture, focusing on workforce satisfaction and development.

text: One area in which we made significant progress during 2016 was external recognition for our commitment to sustainability – whether in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index, Access to Medicine Index, or recognition of our science-based environmental targets. During the year, the Executive team reviewed and refreshed our sustainability strategy.
justification: This argument highlights the company’s commitment to environmental and social responsibility and its progress in sustainability.

text: Our financial results for 2016 were in line with expectations and reflected our ongoing transition. We brought a sharper strategic focus to our three main therapy areas, boosting pipeline productivity further. Our underlying business is growing as the new AstraZeneca emerges, driven by competitive franchises and Emerging Markets.
justification: This argument summarizes the company’s overall financial performance and operational progress during the transition period.

text: 2017 should be a turning point in our journey as we bring new medicines to patients across the globe. It is an exciting time as we approach the inflection point for our anticipated return to long-term growth, built on the foundations of a science-led pipeline.
justification: This argument is a forward-looking statement about the company’s strategic outlook and growth expectations.
